narrativeReportMd:
# MedicationKnowledge R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MedicationKnowledge` is a hard breaking removal in the supplied R6 ballot package: the R4 concrete resource has no same-named R6 core StructureDefinition and no package-index entry. A conformant R6 validator or generated R6 model will not recognize an R4 instance with `resourceType: "MedicationKnowledge"`.

## Scope
The report analyzes the assigned R4 resource and the missing R6 counterpart. It also uses nearby R6 medication/product-definition resources only to assess plausible migration routes. Base-resource and inherited element changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
The main migration issue is not a simple element rename. The old resource mixed medication identifiers, status, manufacturer, dose form, ingredients, monographs, classifications, packaging, clinical-use material, regulatory details, costs, monitoring programs, administration guidance, and kinetics. In R6, some of these concepts have partial homes in `Medication` or product-definition resources, while others have no obvious core successor in the reviewed package. Migration therefore requires domain-specific decomposition, not a lossless mechanical resource rename.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the artifact-level removal (`MedicationKnowledge:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:7a7d10`). Additional high-risk findings cover non-isomorphic split mapping, lost self-reference semantics, status/binding changes, and choice-element/codegen remodeling.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to choose target R6 artifacts and to decide whether lost sections such as cost, monitoring programs, administration guidelines, and kinetics should become extensions, separate definitional resources, implementation-guide profiles, or non-FHIR adjunct data.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive path would have been to keep a deprecated `MedicationKnowledge` resource or publish an official ConceptMap/cross-version extension set. The local package alone does not show whether such a transition artifact exists outside core.

## Follow-up analysis
Follow-up should cover the R6 medication/product-definition resources, removed search parameters, and any official pharmacy module migration guidance.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicationKnowledge` is absent from R6 core, so R4 instances are not R6-core valid as the same resource. Top migration concerns are resource-type removal, split mapping across several R6 resources, and loss or remodeling of knowledge-specific sections. The largest uncertainty is the absence of an official migration map explaining intended successors.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should start by classifying each R4 `MedicationKnowledge` instance: product identity and basic medication properties may map partly to `Medication` and product-definition resources; ingredient details may map to `Medication.ingredient` or `Ingredient`; contraindications/indications may map to `ClinicalUseDefinition`; regulatory authorization details may map to `RegulatedAuthorization`; packaging may map to `Medication.packageSize` or `PackagedProductDefinition`. Several R4 sections, especially cost, monitoring programs, administration guidelines, and kinetics, do not have an obvious one-resource R6 destination in the reviewed core definitions.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same artifact is removed: the named R6 StructureDefinition path is absent, `.index.json` has no `MedicationKnowledge` entry, and package search found no matching artifact. Confidence is medium for the intended replacement analysis because it is inferred from nearby R6 resource structures rather than an official diff, narrative migration page, or ConceptMap.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new artifacts were matched by exact canonical/type/name. The exact R6 artifact is absent. Candidate resources were identified by nearby medication/product naming and overlapping local elements, but no candidate preserves the `MedicationKnowledge` identity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct instance-validation and runtime break. An R4 instance whose `resourceType` is `MedicationKnowledge` has no R6 core StructureDefinition to validate against and no generated R6 resource class in typical code generators. The failure occurs before individual elements are considered.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Medication knowledge may drive medication selection, regulatory interpretation, administration rules, or clinical decision support. Rejecting or mis-mapping the resource can affect medication-reference workflows even if use of this trial-use R4 resource was not universal.

justification.inferredGoal: Move medication knowledge content out of the R4 trial-use resource into R6 medication and product-definition model surfaces.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain MedicationKnowledge in base R6 only as a deprecated compatibility resource while directing new use to the normalized medication/product resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R4 `MedicationKnowledge` was draft/trial-use and FMM 0, and R6 has more focused medication, product, ingredient, clinical-use, and regulatory resources. The complete resource removal is severe, but a fully backward-compatible base design would have required R6 core to continue carrying the obsolete aggregate resource, creating material long-term duplication and implementation burden. That supports `Probably justified`, not fully `Justified`, because the local inputs do not include an official rationale or migration map.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept `MedicationKnowledge` as a deprecated R6 resource with the R4-compatible shape, plus guidance to use newer resources for new implementations. This would preserve most R4-valid instances. The tradeoff is substantial: two core ways to represent overlapping medication knowledge could persist indefinitely, validators and SDKs would still need to support the old model, and implementers might continue using an immature aggregate design instead of the normalized R6 model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy instances but keeps an FMM 0 aggregate model and duplicate medication-knowledge representations in core.

evidence.detail: R4 defines a concrete resource with id/name/type MedicationKnowledge.
The expected R6 StructureDefinition file is absent.
No R6 package index entry was found for MedicationKnowledge.
Several R6 medication/product resources share subsets of the old scope, but none has id/type/url MedicationKnowledge.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment illustrates the root validation problem. R4 permits `MedicationKnowledge` with all local elements optional; R6 core has no resource type by that name.

findings.narrativeMd: `MedicationKnowledge` was a concrete R4 resource, but it is not present in the supplied R6 core package. This is stronger than a rename or cardinality change: an instance cannot even enter normal R6 validation or generated-model deserialization as `MedicationKnowledge`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `MedicationKnowledge` instance becomes R6-invalid because the resource type is unknown to the R6 core package. Strict parsers, validators, schema generators, REST endpoint routing, search parameter registration, and generated SDK classes can all fail before processing element-level content.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not attempt a blind version-label upgrade. Inventory all R4 `MedicationKnowledge` instances, classify their content by use case, and route data to appropriate R6 resources or extensions. Test migration with a validator configured only for R6 core to ensure legacy `resourceType: "MedicationKnowledge"` is no longer emitted unless an implementation-guide-specific compatibility profile is intentionally used.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The most backward-compatible design would have preserved `MedicationKnowledge` in R6, even if deprecated, or provided an official cross-version extension/profile set. That would have allowed old instances to remain syntactically representable while implementers moved to more specific R6 resources. The tradeoff is carrying a draft/FMM 0 model forward.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The identity conclusion is high-confidence; the intended replacement path is not. Review any official pharmacy working-group migration notes before finalizing production transforms.

R6 product-definition resources include formal product, package, manufactured item, and ingredient structures. `ClinicalUseDefinition` and `RegulatedAuthorization` cover some clinical-use and regulatory concepts. facts.note: These may need extensions, implementation-guide profiles, external knowledge artifacts, or manual decomposition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matching was inferred from local element names, definitions, and reference targets in the R6 candidate resources. Because no official cross-version map was supplied, this is a risk finding rather than a definitive element-by-element migration map.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The R4 resource removal is hard breaking, and the content model split creates a high migration risk even after choosing replacement resources. Existing applications that stored one `MedicationKnowledge` document must now create and maintain multiple linked R6 resources, with possible loss of old sections that lack a clear destination.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect decomposition can separate medication facts from regulatory or clinical-use context, which can affect downstream knowledge use.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize a broad R4 knowledge resource into more focused medication, product, ingredient, clinical-use, and regulatory artifacts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated aggregate compatibility resource or wrapper in base R6; a ConceptMap or tooling alone would be migration support, not a base-compatible alternative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Normalizing a broad FMM 0 medication-knowledge resource into focused R6 definitional resources is a plausible goal. However, the report identifies several old content groups with no lossless one-resource destination, and the local package does not show a standard base transition surface. Because the less-breaking base alternative has real duplication costs but the current design leaves substantial mapping ambiguity, this level of breakage is not clearly justified from the available evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `MedicationKnowledge` as a deprecated aggregate resource, possibly with references to the newer product, ingredient, clinical-use, and regulatory resources. That would preserve old instances and give implementations a stable migration target. The tradeoff is material: R6 core would carry both aggregate and normalized representations for overlapping facts, reconciliation rules would be needed when both are present, and the deprecated aggregate might never disappear. A ConceptMap, conversion script, or documentation would help migration but would not itself make R4 instances valid R6 base content.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A compatibility aggregate would reduce loss and ambiguity but would duplicate normalized R6 resources and weaken convergence on the new model.

evidence.detail: R4 differential defines broad local sections including cost, monitoringProgram, administrationGuidelines, medicineClassification, packaging, regulatory, and kinetics.
R6 Medication has only partial overlap: identifier, code, status, marketingAuthorizationHolder, doseForm, packageSize, ingredient, instance, and definition.
R6 candidate resources provide multiple possible targets but no single same-resource replacement.

examples.examplesMd: The example highlights sections that were locally modeled in R4 `MedicationKnowledge` but did not have a direct same-resource R6 destination in the reviewed definitions.

findings.narrativeMd: The deletion is not just a missing class name. `MedicationKnowledge` acted as an aggregate knowledge resource. R6 appears to distribute parts of that aggregate across medication, medicinal-product, ingredient, clinical-use, and regulatory resources. That split is a migration risk because old applications may have relied on one document carrying all knowledge sections together.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation fails at the resource level. Even if a custom transform creates R6 resources, there is no guarantee that every old element has an R6-core representation. Conversely, a set of R6 product-definition resources may not collapse back into one R4 `MedicationKnowledge` instance without selecting and losing information.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit mapping matrix by R4 element group. For each group, define the target R6 resource type, linkage strategy, and loss policy. Treat cost, monitoring programs, administration guidelines, and kinetics as high-priority manual-review buckets because no direct target was identified from the supplied package.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible path could have retained the aggregate resource as a wrapper over newer normalized resources. The benefit would be old-client compatibility and clearer migration; the cost would be continued support for a broad, low-maturity aggregate model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding intentionally groups many old elements rather than emitting a separate removal finding for every local path, because the dominant break is the resource-level split/removal.

findings.title: The local self-reference to MedicationKnowledge has no R6 core target

oldState.summary: R4 allowed each relatedMedicationKnowledge entry to reference one or more MedicationKnowledge resources.
oldState.narrativeMd: `MedicationKnowledge.relatedMedicationKnowledge.reference` was mandatory within each `relatedMedicationKnowledge` backbone and targeted `MedicationKnowledge`.

newState.summary: No R6 MedicationKnowledge resource exists to serve as the target.
newState.narrativeMd: Because the R6 core package has no `MedicationKnowledge` StructureDefinition, this self-reference relationship cannot be carried forward as the same typed reference.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 target is the assigned artifact itself. Since the assigned artifact is absent from R6, the target is removed for core R6.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The containing resource is already removed, but this local reference target creates an additional graph-migration risk. Systems that linked medication-knowledge records to other medication-knowledge records must choose a new relationship model among R6 product-definition or knowledge resources.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly dropping related-knowledge links can lose association semantics such as branded/generic or related documentation relationships.

justification.inferredGoal: Eliminate the old aggregate knowledge graph in favor of more specific R6 definitional resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Preserve the old self-reference only by retaining a deprecated MedicationKnowledge target or by adding a standard successor-resource relationship with incomplete coverage.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Once the aggregate resource is removed, the self-reference target cannot remain as a normal R6 core reference. The likely goal of moving relationship modeling to more specific product or knowledge resources is reasonable. A less-breaking design exists only as part of a broader compatibility resource or by adding relationship elements to successor resources, both of which create overlapping graph patterns, so the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest backward-compatible base alternative would be to keep deprecated `MedicationKnowledge` resources addressable so existing `relatedMedicationKnowledge.reference` links still resolve. A weaker alternative would add a standard relationship element on successor resources. The first preserves R4 instances but inherits the full duplicate-resource burden; the second helps migrated data but does not preserve R4 instances unchanged and may overlap with R6 product cross-reference features. A ConceptMap or local extension is useful migration guidance, not by itself a backward-compatible base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old graph links but duplicates relationship semantics and may conflict with newer product cross-reference structures.

evidence.detail: R4 targetProfile is MedicationKnowledge and min cardinality is 1 within the backbone.
No R6 target StructureDefinition exists for MedicationKnowledge.

examples.examplesMd: The reference syntax itself is standard R4, but in R6 core the target resource type is absent.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 could model a graph of related medication-knowledge records. Removing the resource also removes the local target type for those graph edges, so a migration must decide whether links become product cross-references, related `Medication` resources, documentation links, or extensions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance using this reference is not R6-core valid because the root resource is unknown. If transformed into R6 candidate resources, the reference cannot be preserved as `Reference(MedicationKnowledge)` and may fail typed-reference validation or generated-model type checks.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory uses of `relatedMedicationKnowledge`. For each relation type, define a target R6 relation pattern and include tests for reference resolution, graph traversal, and reverse lookup. Do not silently drop relations unless a domain owner confirms they are non-essential.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping a deprecated target resource or defining a standard relation extension would have preserved old graph semantics while allowing newer resources to carry forward relationships. Without that, migrations are necessarily policy-driven.

findings.title: MedicationKnowledge.status uses a removed value set and only partially aligns with R6 status semantics

oldState.summary: R4 status is an optional modifier code with required binding to medicationknowledge-status.

binding.description: A coded concept defining if the medication is in active use.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: The medication is available for use.
changedCodes.newMeaning: R6 Medication.status active means the medication record is current and appropriate for reference in new instances.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Same lexical code but different code system and more record-oriented definition in R6 Medication.status.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: The medication is not available for use.
changedCodes.newMeaning: R6 Medication.status inactive means the medication record is not current and is not appropriate for reference in new instances.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Same lexical code but different code system and altered record-currency wording.

changedCodes.oldMeaning: The medication was entered in error.
changedCodes.newMeaning: R6 Medication.status entered-in-error means the medication record was created erroneously and is not appropriate for reference in new instances.
changedCodes.changeSummary: Same lexical code but different code system and altered record-oriented wording.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The compared CodeSystems have the same three lexical codes, but the R6 package has no `medicationknowledge-status`; likely R6 mappings must either use `Medication.status` or a product-definition publication status, which is not semantically identical.

flags.isModifierReason: This element changes the interpretation of all descriptive attributes.

oldState.narrativeMd: `MedicationKnowledge.status` modified interpretation of all descriptive attributes and was bound to a MedicationKnowledge-specific required value set.

newState.summary: No R6 MedicationKnowledge.status exists. Candidate R6 statuses use either Medication.status with a different value set/code system or product-definition publication statuses.

binding.description: R6 Medication.status required binding if mapping to Medication.

newState.narrativeMd: `Medication.status` preserves lexical codes but uses `http://hl7.org/fhir/CodeSystem/medication-status` and record-current semantics. Product-definition resources often use publication-status style bindings, so `inactive` and `entered-in-error` do not map uniformly across all plausible R6 targets.

facts.note: Overlap helps if mapping specifically to Medication.status, but the canonical system and definitions differ.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 candidate was matched by element name and code set on `Medication.status`, not by same artifact identity. Product-definition status elements are also plausible but use different status models.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The resource removal is the hard break. At the status-element level, lexical values may be reusable for `Medication.status`, but terminology canonical, modifier scope, and status semantics change. Mapping the same string to all R6 targets would be unsafe.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Status controls whether knowledge is active or erroneous; misinterpreting it can expose inactive or erroneous medication facts.

justification.inferredGoal: Align medication status with the R6 medication/product model rather than retaining a MedicationKnowledge-specific status system.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the old MedicationKnowledge status binding only inside a deprecated compatibility resource; terminology maps are mitigation, not a base-compatible design.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning status with R6 `Medication` and product-definition status patterns is reasonable, especially because the old resource and value set were tied to a trial-use aggregate model. The lexical codes overlap for `Medication.status`, but the canonical terminology and modifier scope differ, and product-definition statuses are not uniformly equivalent. A less-breaking base option exists only if the old resource/status binding is retained, which has material duplicate-model costs; therefore the break is probably justified but still needs careful migration mapping.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The base-compatible alternative would be to keep `MedicationKnowledge.status` with its R4 required binding on a deprecated R6 `MedicationKnowledge` resource, while new R6 resources use their own status elements. That preserves old instances and old modifier semantics. The tradeoff is that R6 would maintain two status models for overlapping medication knowledge, and implementers would need rules for translating or reconciling them. A ConceptMap or retained alias ValueSet can reduce migration risk, but it does not make the old resource or old binding a native R6 base instance shape.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the old binding preserves modifier semantics for legacy data but maintains duplicate status models and can confuse target-resource status interpretation.

evidence.detail: R4 status is optional, modifier=true, summary=true, code type, and required-bound to medicationknowledge-status|4.0.1.
R4 code system defines active, inactive, and entered-in-error.
R6 Medication.status is optional, modifier=true, summary=true, and required-bound to medication-status|6.0.0-ballot4.
R6 medication-status uses the same three lexical codes but different system and record-current definitions.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is only safe when the target is R6 `Medication.status`; it is not a general mapping for all candidate product-definition resources.

findings.narrativeMd: The status value looks deceptively easy because the common values are still `active`, `inactive`, and `entered-in-error` on R6 `Medication.status`. However, the old `MedicationKnowledge` value set is absent and product-definition resources use different status patterns. A string-level transform can therefore be semantically wrong.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `MedicationKnowledge.status` is not directly R6-valid because the containing resource is gone. If transformed to `Medication.status`, the lexical code may validate but the terminology system and modifier scope change. If transformed to product-definition status, the value may not validate or may require a different CodeableConcept/status model.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map status per target resource, not globally. Preserve the old status source in audit/provenance or an extension when the target status semantics are not equivalent. Include test cases for all three R4 status codes and for absent status.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A formal ConceptMap from `medicationknowledge-status` to each candidate R6 status element would have avoided ambiguous string reuse. Retaining the old ValueSet as a compatibility alias would also reduce terminology failures but would not solve resource removal.

findings.title: R4 choice elements and generated classes cannot be carried forward mechanically

oldState.summary: R4 MedicationKnowledge uses several local choice elements with R4 JSON choice-property names.

newState.summary: No R6 MedicationKnowledge choice elements exist; partial candidate mappings use different representations such as CodeableReference or separate resources.
newState.narrativeMd: For example, R6 `Medication.ingredient.item` is a `CodeableReference` rather than R4 `itemCodeableConcept`/`itemReference`, and other old choice concepts may land in `ClinicalUseDefinition`, `Ingredient`, product-definition property elements, extensions, or not at all.

facts.note: Candidate paths are not one-to-one replacements for the old properties.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The choice-element issue is inferred from old local choice definitions and the structure of candidate R6 resources. No same-resource R6 choice set exists.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Generated R4 model properties and FHIRPath expressions over old choice names will not compile or evaluate against R6 candidate resources. Even where a semantic analogue exists, the JSON shape changes from R4 choice property names to R6 CodeableReference or separate-resource structures.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ingredient, indication, patient characteristic, and drug characteristic details can affect medication knowledge interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Use newer R6 modeling patterns such as CodeableReference and specialized definitional resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Preserve legacy choice JSON only by keeping the old resource/fields; transforms or extensions reduce migration pain but are not base compatibility.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using R6 modeling patterns such as `CodeableReference` and specialized definitional resources is a reasonable goal. FHIR JSON cannot cleanly treat old R4 choice-arm property names as aliases for a different R6 element without creating duplicate same-resource representations. Because the less-breaking base design would require retaining the old choice fields, most likely as part of a deprecated compatibility resource, the break is probably justified despite its high code-generation impact.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The only base design that preserves old generated fields such as `itemCodeableConcept`, `itemReference`, and `valueQuantity` is to keep those old choice elements in a deprecated R6 `MedicationKnowledge` shape or to add duplicate legacy fields beside newer R6 structures. That would preserve R4 instances but introduce validation ambiguity and long-lived duplicate representations for the same facts. Official transforms and regression fixtures are valuable mitigations, but they are not a backward-compatible base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Legacy aliases would preserve generated-code compatibility but create duplicate representations and validation ambiguity around CodeableReference and newer resource structures.

evidence.detail: R4 defines local choice elements for ingredient item, administration indication, patient characteristic, and drug characteristic value.
R6 Medication.ingredient.item is CodeableReference with Substance, SubstanceDefinition, and Medication targets.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example only covers one candidate mapping for ingredient details. It does not preserve all R4 `MedicationKnowledge` choice elements.

findings.narrativeMd: Choice elements are a code-generation hazard. R4 SDKs often generate separate fields such as `itemCodeableConcept` and `itemReference`; R6 candidate structures may generate a single `CodeableReference` field or entirely different resources. Code that appears to be field-level migration will fail unless it handles each old choice arm explicitly.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old choice-property names are not valid R6 JSON under any same-named resource because no same-named resource exists. When mapping to candidate resources, validators will expect R6 property names and R6 type domains. R6 content using `CodeableReference` is not directly representable in R4 `MedicationKnowledge` without choosing a concept/reference arm and possibly dropping additional target choices.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build tests for every old choice arm and every candidate R6 type. Avoid string-based property renames; use a typed transform that understands CodeableReference, Reference target changes, and when information must become an extension or separate resource.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: FHIR version changes normally cannot keep two JSON shapes for the same element. The reasonable compatibility alternative would be official cross-version transform definitions and regression fixtures. Without them, implementers must design and validate transforms independently.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The gap assessment is based on R4 local element definitions and top-level/nearby R6 candidate resource review. A deeper narrative-page or ConceptMap review could identify intended targets not obvious from the core StructureDefinitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These sections can contain clinically or operationally important knowledge. Resource removal makes the old instance invalid, and the absence of obvious target fields makes automated migration lossy unless a site-specific representation is chosen.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Administration guidance, monitoring programs, and kinetic data can affect safe medication use; cost can affect formulary/business decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid carrying specialized knowledge sections in a broad medication knowledge resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the removed knowledge sections in a deprecated compatibility resource or add standard base targets for them; extensions/profiles alone are incomplete mitigations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Avoiding broad, specialized knowledge sections in a low-maturity aggregate resource is a plausible R6 goal. The available evidence, however, does not show direct R6 core destinations for cost, monitoring programs, administration guidance, and kinetics, some of which can be clinically or operationally important. Because a less-breaking base design could have preserved these sections but with material modeling and duplication costs, the current breakage is not clearly justified from the local package evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept these sections on a deprecated `MedicationKnowledge` resource or introduced explicit standard R6 base elements/resources for the major concepts. That would preserve old data and reduce silent-loss risk. The tradeoff is substantial: it would continue carrying a broad knowledge model in core, may overlap with `ClinicalUseDefinition`, product-definition properties, or knowledge-artifact resources, and would require clear reconciliation guidance. Standard extensions or IG profiles are useful mitigations but do not fully preserve base R6 interoperability or unchanged R4 instance validity.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves clinically important data but keeps broad knowledge content in core and may duplicate specialized knowledge-artifact models.

evidence.detail: R4 contains local structures for cost, monitoring program, administration guidelines, and kinetics.

evidence.locator: top-level and relevant differential element review
evidence.detail: The reviewed R6 medication/product-definition candidates did not provide direct same-named or obviously equivalent elements for these groups.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows knowledge-specific sections that should not be dropped without domain review.

findings.narrativeMd: Some parts of R4 `MedicationKnowledge` are not just definitional product fields. They can encode guidance, monitoring, cost, and kinetic knowledge. The reviewed R6 candidate resources do not make a direct replacement obvious, so these sections are especially vulnerable to silent data loss.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using these sections are invalid as R6 core `MedicationKnowledge`. Mapping them into R6 may require extensions or other resources. If an implementation simply maps product identity and ingredients, these sections can be lost while the transformed data appears otherwise valid.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Flag instances containing these sections for manual or rules-based enrichment. Decide whether administration guidance should become a knowledge artifact such as `PlanDefinition`, `ActivityDefinition`, `Library`, or an extension; decide whether kinetics and cost have local extension profiles. Include loss reports in migration output.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A standard set of extensions for removed knowledge-specific sections would have been less disruptive than requiring every implementer to invent local mappings. The cost is that extensions would not have the same interoperability as core elements.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No R4 local `MedicationKnowledge` differential element had a fixed value, pattern, or default value. The R6 resource is absent, so there is no separate fixed/pattern/default-value break beyond resource removal.
No local R4 `MedicationKnowledge` slicing was identified in the assigned StructureDefinition. No slicing-specific local finding was needed.
No local R4 `MedicationKnowledge` element used maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints that required a separate finding. The dominant validation break is artifact absence.
No MedicationKnowledge-specific invariant change could be compared because the R6 counterpart is absent. Inherited `ele-*`, `ext-*`, and `dom-*` constraints are intentionally out of scope.
The local R4 modifier element `MedicationKnowledge.status` is covered in the terminology/status finding. Inherited modifierExtension and implicitRules behavior is out of scope.
R4 summary flags were checked for local elements. Because the R6 resource is absent, summary behavior changes are subsumed by resource removal rather than a separate summary-flag-only break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 contains partial analogue resources for some MedicationKnowledge concepts
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The existence of R6 `Medication`, product-definition resources, `Ingredient`, `ClinicalUseDefinition`, and `RegulatedAuthorization` is not itself a breaking change to `MedicationKnowledge`; the break is the absence of a same-identity resource.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: These resources are likely starting points for migration design, but they should be analyzed separately and should not be treated as a single automatic successor.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R4 status lexical codes overlap with R6 Medication.status
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The lexical code overlap (`active`, `inactive`, `entered-in-error`) can reduce migration friction if a specific instance maps to R6 `Medication.status`; it does not remove the resource-level break or the status semantic/canonical differences.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Do not use lexical overlap as proof of semantic equivalence across all R6 target resources.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: The removed R4 resource was draft/trial-use and FMM 0
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Maturity status does not change instance validity by itself, but it explains why a major model change may have been considered acceptable by the specification process.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers that adopted this low-maturity R4 resource should expect more manual migration work than for normative resources.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot note, or pharmacy work-group migration rationale was available in the supplied inputs. This limits confidence about intended replacement resources and whether compatibility artifacts exist outside core.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official FHIR change logs, Jira tickets, pharmacy module notes, and any cross-version maps for MedicationKnowledge.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`) and may change before publication. The finding is accurate for the supplied package but should be rechecked against the final R6 package.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Repeat the package-index and StructureDefinition search against the final R6 core package.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Only the material status CodeSystems/ValueSets were inspected directly. Example/preferred bindings for dose form, routes, package type, characteristics, and product-definition candidates were not expanded or compared.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No real-world or official example corpus was analyzed, so expected prevalence of individual sections such as cost, monitoring programs, administration guidelines, and kinetics is unknown.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Analyze production or published R4 MedicationKnowledge instances to quantify which old sections are used and prioritize migration rules.
